title: Layers and compositing
purpose: Reconstructs the layer stack back to front, opacity, blend, edges, masks and depth cues so the composite can be rebuilt from new assets.
boundary: The swarm lifts technique and structure only. Never store, transcribe or reuse the source's footage, frames, music, voice or script text. Keyframes and spectrograms are temporary analysis files in a scratch directory and are never copied into the format IR or a variant. On-screen text may be quoted only as a locating note in evidence.note, at most 6 words, and narration is never quoted. Patterns replace content words with slots, e.g. 'FACT {n}' or '{number} {unit} {noun}'. Analysing a public video for technique is fine; republishing its content is not.
inspect: F3 crops at panel and inset edges, F9 average colour inside a panel over two different backgrounds to estimate opacity, F2 bursts to see which layers move.
pitfalls: Calling a layer semi-transparent without seeing a background change through it
Counting a texture baked into a photo as a separate layer
Guessing blend modes; say 'unknown' unless the behaviour shows it

methods.measured: A measurement tool produced the value (an evidence.json field or an ffmpeg/ffprobe filter output). Name the tool and the field.
methods.observed: You looked at extracted frames, crops, scopes, spectrograms or waveforms and saw it. Give the timestamps you looked at.
methods.inferred: Reasoned from measured or observed facts, e.g. 'synthetic voice' from flat pitch on a spectrogram. State the reasoning in the note.
methods.assumed: No direct evidence; a default or convention. Use only for gaps the format needs filled, and keep confidence at 0.3 or lower.

pointer_conventions: ir_path is a JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) into the Video format IR (contract schema video_re_format_ir).
A final '/-' means 'append this answer to the array' (the RFC 6901 end-of-array token), e.g. /motion/transitions/- or /generation_rules/-.
A '*' segment means 'each array element the answer is about'; the answer must say which elements (for example beats with role 'item'). The lifter resolves '*' to concrete indexes.
Paths under free-form objects (typography.title, typography.captions, typography.labels, audio.narration, audio.music, render_binding.mapping) use the snake_case key named in the question.

answer_types.number: {"value": n, "unit": "..."} optionally with "min" and "max"; becomes an IR observed_number
answer_types.enum: exactly one of the question's choices (a string)
answer_types.list: array of short strings (technique names or kinds)
answer_types.timestamps: array of seconds from the start of the source
answer_types.layers: array of IR layer objects (z, kind, opacity, optional blend, motion, feather_px, frame_coverage, source_slot)
answer_types.parameter: one IR parameter object (name, type, description, default, min/max or choices, derived_from)
answer_types.object: a JSON object with the keys the question's how_to_answer names

recipes.F2: Burst sheet, 10 frames over 1 s: ffmpeg -v error -ss T -t 1 -i "$SRC" -vf "fps=10,scale=270:-2,tile=5x2" -frames:v 1 "$WORK/burst_T.jpg"
recipes.F3: Full-resolution crop (add ,scale=iw*2:-1:flags=lanczos to enlarge): ffmpeg -v error -ss T -i "$SRC" -frames:v 1 -vf "crop=W:H:X:Y" "$WORK/crop_T.png"
recipes.F5: Per-frame motion in a region (mean absolute frame difference, 0-255): ffmpeg -v error -i "$SRC" -vf "crop=iw:ih*0.15:0:0,tblend=all_mode=difference,signalstats,metadata=mode=print:key=lavfi.signalstats.YAVG:file=$WORK/diff.txt" -an -f null -  (drop the crop for the full frame)
recipes.F8: Every frame in a short window (animation timing; frame k is at T + k/fps): ffmpeg -v error -ss T -t 0.5 -i "$SRC" -vf "scale=540:-2" "$WORK/step_T_%03d.png"
recipes.F9: Average colour of a region: ffmpeg -v error -ss T -i "$SRC" -frames:v 1 -vf "crop=W:H:X:Y,scale=1:1:flags=area,format=rgb24" -f rawvideo - | od -An -tu1

questions.question: How many distinct visual layers are stacked in a typical item shot?
questions.why_it_matters: Sets n_layers and checks a layered-look requirement.
questions.how_to_answer: On F1 frames from 3 item shots, list separable elements back to front (background, grid or texture, light, particles, photo, panel, text, vignette); confirm separate layers by different motion on an F2 burst.
questions.challenge: Elements that never move independently and have no transparency could be one baked image; require a motion or opacity cue per counted layer.

questions.question: What is the layer stack from back to front, with each layer's kind?
questions.why_it_matters: Fills visual.layers, the core of the composite recipe.
questions.how_to_answer: Order layers by occlusion: whatever covers another is above it. Use F3 crops where elements overlap.
questions.challenge: Check each ordering claim at one overlap crop; a layer above text must actually cover text.

questions.question: Which layers are semi-transparent, and what is each one's estimated opacity?
questions.why_it_matters: Fills opacity per layer; a common rule caps every layer below 100%.
questions.how_to_answer: Sample a layer's colour (F9) at the same spot over two different underlying backgrounds; with known background colours B1, B2 and observed O1, O2, opacity a = 1 - (O1 - O2)/(B1 - B2) per channel. Report per layer.
evidence_required: frames: F9 samples over two backgrounds
questions.challenge: If the background did not change under the layer, opacity cannot be measured; method must drop to observed or inferred.

questions.question: What does the overlay transparency probe report, and does frame inspection agree?
questions.why_it_matters: Ties the measured semi_transparent_ratio to specific layers.
questions.how_to_answer: Read evidence.overlay.semi_transparent_ratio (video_re_overlay_transparency_probe); compare with the layers judged semi-transparent in 003.
questions.challenge: Read the probe's definition before interpreting the ratio; never treat it as an opacity value.

questions.question: Which blend modes are visible (screen-like brightening, multiply-like darkening, overlay contrast, plain alpha)?
questions.why_it_matters: Fills blend per layer.
questions.how_to_answer: For light, haze and texture layers, check whether dark areas stay dark under them (screen/add) or light areas stay light (multiply), on F3 crops.
evidence_required: frames: F3 crops of light and texture layers
questions.challenge: Anything not demonstrated by such a test must be 'unknown'.

questions.question: How is depth implied (blur on far layers, scale difference, parallax, drop shadows, haze, overlap)?
questions.why_it_matters: Becomes depth rules for the compositor.
questions.how_to_answer: List cues seen on F1 frames and F2 bursts, each with a timestamp.
questions.challenge: Each cue needs a timestamp where it is visible.

questions.question: How are the edges of inset media treated (feathered, hard, rounded, stroked, shadowed)?
questions.why_it_matters: Fills edge treatment; hard rectangular cut-outs are a known failure in this project.
questions.how_to_answer: F3 enlarged crops at the edges of the main photo in 3 shots.
questions.challenge: Check all four edges in one shot; feathering only at the bottom is a gradient mask, not a feather.

questions.question: How wide is the feather (soft edge) in pixels at full resolution?
questions.why_it_matters: Fills feather_px.
questions.how_to_answer: On an F3 crop across an edge, count pixels from where the photo starts to fade to where the background is fully visible.
evidence_required: frames: F3 edge crops at full resolution
questions.challenge: Measure on two edges; report both values.

questions.question: Is there a frosted or blurred panel behind text, and how strong are its blur and tint?
questions.why_it_matters: Adds a frosted-panel layer with parameters.
questions.how_to_answer: F3 crop of the panel: blurred background detail visible through it indicates frosted glass; estimate tint opacity with the method from 003.
questions.challenge: A solid plate has no visible background detail; check over a busy background.

questions.question: How is the frame filled when media does not cover it (blurred copy, gradient, solid colour, pattern)?
questions.why_it_matters: Becomes the fill strategy.
questions.how_to_answer: Inspect the areas outside the main media on F1 frames.
questions.challenge: Make sure the fill is not a separate background system (answered by that lens).

questions.question: Is there a vignette, and how much darker are the corners than the centre?
questions.why_it_matters: Adds a vignette layer with strength.
questions.how_to_answer: F9 average colour of a 5% corner crop versus the central 20% on a frame with even content; report the luma ratio.
questions.challenge: Content that is naturally dark at the edges can fake a vignette; check two different shots.

questions.question: Is there a grain or noise overlay, and is it static or animated?
questions.why_it_matters: Adds a grain layer.
questions.how_to_answer: F3 crop of a flat area enlarged 4x on two consecutive frames (F8); animated grain changes per frame.
evidence_required: frames: F3 and F8 on a flat region
questions.challenge: Compression noise is blocky and follows macroblocks; true grain is fine and uniform.

questions.question: Are light leaks, flares or light sweeps overlaid, and how often?
questions.why_it_matters: Adds a light layer with frequency.
questions.how_to_answer: Find warm or bright moving patches not tied to scene content on F2 bursts; list timestamps.
questions.challenge: A real sun flare in footage is not an overlay; it must also cover graphics or text-only frames.

questions.question: Is there a particle, dust or bokeh layer, and how dense and fast is it?
questions.why_it_matters: Adds a particles layer.
questions.how_to_answer: F2 bursts on a darker region; count particles per frame and estimate drift speed.
questions.challenge: Report a count; 'some particles' is not an answer.

questions.question: Is any visual layer fully opaque over the whole frame for more than a second?
questions.why_it_matters: Checks the opacity cap rule; full-frame opaque layers hide the background system.
questions.how_to_answer: Look for frames where nothing from the background shows through (F1); check border motion (F5) during those times.
questions.challenge: Full-bleed photos are opaque by nature; say whether the format places them full-frame.

questions.question: Do cut-out subjects or panels cast drop shadows, and what are the offset and blur?
questions.why_it_matters: Adds shadow parameters.
questions.how_to_answer: F3 crop under a cut-out; measure shadow offset and blur radius in px.
questions.challenge: Report px values; a 'soft shadow' alone is incomplete.

questions.question: Are subjects cut out from their backgrounds or shown as rectangular images?
questions.why_it_matters: Decides whether background removal is part of the pipeline.
questions.how_to_answer: Inspect subject edges on F3 crops.
questions.challenge: Feathered rectangles are not cut-outs; cut-outs follow the subject's outline.

questions.question: What mask shapes are used (circle, rounded rectangle, gradient fade, custom shape)?
questions.why_it_matters: Adds mask types to the layer recipe.
questions.how_to_answer: Inspect inset media and reveals on F1 and F3.
questions.challenge: List one timestamp per mask type.

questions.question: Does the number or type of layers change between beats (for example more overlays in the hook)?
questions.why_it_matters: Becomes a per-beat layer rule.
questions.how_to_answer: Repeat the layer count (001) on hook, item and outro frames.
questions.challenge: Count per beat role, not per shot.

questions.question: Are there colour tint overlays (a solid colour at low opacity over everything)?
questions.why_it_matters: Adds a tint layer and its colour.
questions.how_to_answer: Compare neutral elements (white text, grey areas) for a uniform colour shift using F9.
questions.challenge: A grade and a tint overlay look similar; a tint also affects text drawn above the grade only if it sits above the text.

questions.question: Is there a grid of moving panels (for example 2x2) behind or around the main visual?
questions.why_it_matters: Adds a grid-2x2 layer kind.
questions.how_to_answer: Look for repeated rectangles with independent motion on F2 bursts.
questions.challenge: Static grid lines belong to a grid layer, not a panel grid; check that panels move independently.

questions.question: Is there glow or bloom around bright elements or text?
questions.why_it_matters: Adds a glow effect.
questions.how_to_answer: F3 crop around bright text; a halo of raised brightness beyond the stroke indicates glow.
questions.challenge: Compression ringing produces thin halos; glow is wider (several px) and smooth.

questions.question: What compositing artefacts appear (halo edges, aliasing, hard rectangular patches, banding) that a rebuild must avoid?
questions.why_it_matters: Becomes negative rules (things the compositor must not do).
questions.how_to_answer: Inspect F3 crops at edges and gradients; list artefacts with timestamps.
questions.challenge: Every artefact needs a timestamp and region.

questions.question: Which layers move during a shot and which are static?
questions.why_it_matters: Fills motion per layer.
questions.how_to_answer: Compare F2 burst frames: elements whose position or content changes move.
questions.challenge: Camera moves move everything; describe per-layer motion relative to the frame.

questions.question: Does any text sit behind a subject (subject occludes text) for a depth effect?
questions.why_it_matters: Adds an occlusion option to the layer order.
questions.how_to_answer: Look for frames where part of the title or label is covered by a subject's outline (F3).
questions.challenge: Text cropped by a panel edge is not occlusion by a subject.

questions.question: Are there border or frame layers (film frame, polaroid, phone mock-up, outline)?
questions.why_it_matters: Adds a border layer.
questions.how_to_answer: Inspect frame edges and inset media on F1.
questions.challenge: Say whether the frame is constant or changes per item.

questions.question: Which layers are fixed for the whole video and which change per item (slots)?
questions.why_it_matters: Separates template layers from content layers for the parameteriser.
questions.how_to_answer: Compare the layer list (002) across items.
questions.challenge: A layer whose asset changes but whose style stays is a slot, not fixed.

questions.question: What should max_layer_opacity and n_layers be as parameters, with ranges from the evidence?
questions.why_it_matters: Turns observed values into parameters.
questions.how_to_answer: Use the maximum observed opacity (003) and the layer count range across beats (019).
questions.challenge: The parameter default must equal an observed value.

questions.question: What is the estimated opacity of text backing panels?
questions.why_it_matters: Fills panel opacity for captions and titles.
questions.how_to_answer: Apply the two-background method from 003 to the caption panel at two times with different underlying images.
evidence_required: frames: F9 panel samples at two times
questions.challenge: If the panel is blurred (frosted), the blur changes the underlying colour; sample flat areas.

questions.question: Do layers align to consistent margins (for example all insets 64 px from the frame edge)?
questions.why_it_matters: Adds margin constants to the render binding.
questions.how_to_answer: Measure insets' distances to the frame edges on 4 frames.
questions.challenge: Report measured px; consistency needs at most 2% spread.

questions.question: Is the composite built as 2.5D (layers separated in depth with perspective or scale by depth)?
questions.why_it_matters: Selects a 2.5D compositor or plain 2D stacking.
questions.how_to_answer: Look for layers that scale or shift differently during moves (F1 start/end) and for perspective distortion.
questions.challenge: Independent animations are not depth; depth needs a consistent relation between scale and motion.

questions.question: Are chromatic aberration, RGB split or scanline overlays used, and where?
questions.why_it_matters: Adds stylised overlay effects.
questions.how_to_answer: F3 crops at high-contrast edges for colour fringes; F2 bursts for flicker.
questions.challenge: Lens fringing in footage is not an effect; it must also appear on graphics.

questions.question: Do overlays (light, particles, grain) sit above or below the text?
questions.why_it_matters: Fixes the z-order of overlays relative to text.
questions.how_to_answer: Check whether overlay elements cross over letters on F3 crops.
questions.challenge: Find one frame where an overlay element and a letter overlap; without it the answer is not determinable.
